m: 1. कृष् cl. 1. P. कर्षति, rarely Ā. ˚ते (perf. चकर्ष, 2. sg. ˚षिथ, Pāṇ. vii, 2, 62, Kāś.; fut. कर्क्ष्यति or क्रक्ष्य्˚; कृषिष्य्˚, Divyāv. xvii; कर्ष्टा or क्रष्टा, Pāṇ. vii, 2, 10, Kāś.; aor. अकृक्षत् [or अकार्क्षीत्] or अक्राक्षीत्, iii, 1, 44, Vārtt. 7; inf. क्रष्टुम्), to draw, draw to one's self, drag, pull, drag away, tear, RV.; AV.; ŚBr. &c.; to lead or conduct (as an army), MBh.; to bend (a bow), Ragh. v, 50; to draw into one's power, become master of, overpower, Mn. ii, 215; MBh. iv, 20; R.; Pañcat.; to obtain, Mn. iii, 66; to take away anything (acc.) from any one (acc.), Vop. v, 8; to draw or make furrows, plough, RV. viii, 22, 6; Lāṭy. v, 1, 4; Vait. (Ā.), R. iii, 4, 12; BhP. (ind.p. कृष्ट्वा) : cl. 6. P. Ā. कृषति, ˚ते (p. कृषत्), to draw or make furrows, plough, RV.; AV.; TS.; ŚBr. &c.; Ā. to obtain by ploughing, AV. xii, 2, 16; to travel over, MBh. iii, 16021 : Caus. कर्षयति, to draw, drag, RV. x, 119, 11 (aor. 1. sg. अचिकृषम्), R.; Mṛcch.; to draw or tear out, MBh. iii, 2307; to pull to and fro, cause pain, torture, torment, Mn.; MBh. &c.; ‘to plough’, see कर्षित: Intens. (pr. p. and Subj. 3. sg. चर्कृषत्; impf. 3. pl. अचर्कृषुर्) to plough, RV.; AV.; चरीकृष्यते or Ved. करीक्˚, to plough repeatedly, Pāṇ. vii, 4, 64;
कृष् [cf. Lith. karszu, pleszau; Russ. česhu; Lat. verro, vello; Goth. falh.]
2. कृष् mfn. See कंस-क्˚.
a: कृष् — {vI.v} {c6c} U. (कृषति-ते, कृष्ट) To plough, make furrows. {vII.v} {c1c} P. (कर्षति, कृष्ट) 1 To draw, drag, pull, drag away, tear; प्रसह्य सिंहः किल तां चकर्ष R. 2. 27; V. 1. 19. --2 To draw towards oneself, attract; Bk. 15. 47; Bg. 15. 7. --3 To lead or conduct as an army; स सेनां महतीं कर्षन् R. 4. 32. --4 To bend (as a bow); {{नात्यायतष्टकृशांर्गः->नात्यायतकृष्टशार्ंगः||20180518|||छोनृइर्म् आफ्-1957, फ्ठ्घ्}} R. 5. 50. --5 To be come master of, subdue, vanquish, overpower; बलवानिंद्रियग्रामो विद्वांसमपि कर्षति Ms. 2. 215; नक्रः स्वस्थानमासाद्य गजेंद्रमपि कर्षति Pt. 3. 46. --6 To plough, till; अनुलोमकृष्टं क्षेत्रं प्रतिलोमं कर्षति Sk. --7 To obtain; कुलसंख्यां च गच्छंति कर्षंति च महद्यशः Mb. --8 To take away from, deprive one of (with two acc.). --Caus. 1 To draw out, tear up. --2 To extract. --3 To torture, torment, give pain. --4 To plough, till, cultivate.

N. of a celebrated Avatār of the god Viṣṇu, or sometimes identified with Viṣṇu himself [MBh. v, 2563; xiv, 1589 ff.; Hariv. 2359 &c.] as distinct from his ten Avatārs or incarnations (in the earlier legends he appears as a great hero and teacher [MBh.; Bhag.]; in the more recent he is deified, and is often represented as a young and amorous shepherd with flowing hair and a flute in his hand; the following are a few particulars of his birth and history as related in Hariv. 3304 ff. and in the Purāṇas &c.: Vasu-deva, who was a descendant of Yadu and Yayāti, had two wives, Rohiṇī and Devakī; the latter had eight sons of whom the eighth was Kṛṣṇa; Kaṃsa, king of Mathurā and cousin of Devakī, was informed by a prediction that one of these sons would kill him; he therefore kept Vasu-deva and his wife in confinement, and slew their first six children; the seventh was Balarāma who was saved by being abstracted from the womb of Devakī and transferred to that of Rohiṇī; the eighth was Kṛṣṇa who was born with black skin and a peculiar mark on his breast; his father Vasu-deva managed to escape from Mathurā with the child, and favoured by the gods found a herdsman named Nanda whose wife Yaśo-dā had just been delivered of a son which Vasu-deva conveyed to Devakī after substituting his own in its place. Nanda with his wife Yaśo-dā took the infant Kṛṣṇa and settled first in Gokula or Vraja, and afterwards in Vṛndāvana, where Kṛṣṇa and Bala-rāma grew up together, roaming in the woods and joining in the sports of the herdsmen's sons ; Kṛṣṇa as a youth contested the sovereignty of Indra, and was victorious over that god, who descended from heaven to praise Kṛṣṇa, and made him lord over the cattle [Hariv. 3787 ff.; 7456 ff.; VP.]; Kṛṣṇa is described as sporting constantly with the Gopīs or shepherdesses [Hariv. 4078 ff.; 8301 ff.; VP.; Gīt.] of whom a thousand became his wives, though only eight are specified, Rādhā being the favourite [Hariv. 6694 ff.; 9177 ff.; VP.]; Kṛṣṇa built and fortified a city called Dvārakā in Gujarāt, and thither transported the inhabitants of Mathurā after killing Kaṃsa; Kṛṣṇa had various wives besides the Gopīs, and by Rukmiṇī had a son Pradyumna who is usually identified with Kāma-deva; with Jains, Kṛṣṇa is one of the nine black Vasu-devas; with Buddhists he is the chief of the black demons, who are the enemies of Buddha and the white demons)

[कृष्-नक्] 1 Black, dark, dark-blue. --2 Wicked, evil. --ष्णः 1 The black colour. --2 The black antelope. --3 A crow. --4 The (Indian) cuckoo. --5 The dark half of a lunar month (from full to new moon). --6 The Kali age. --7 Viṣṇu in his eighth incarnation, born as the son of Vasudeva and Devakī. [Kṛṣṇa is the most celebrated hero of Indian mythology and the most popular of all the deities. Though the real son of Vasudeva and Devakī and thus a cousin of Kaṃsa, he was, for all practical purposes, the son of Nanda and Yaśodā by whom he was brought up and in whose house he spent his childhood. It was here that his divine character began to be gradually discovered, when he easily crushed the most redoubtable demons, such as Baka, Pūtanā &c., that were sent to kill him by Kaṃsa, and performed many other feats of surprising strength. The chief companions of his youth were the Gopīs or wives of the cowherds of Gokula, among whom Rādhā was his special favourite; (cf. Jayadeva's Gītagovinda). He killed Kaṃsa, Naraka, Keśin, Ariṣṭa and a host of other powerful demons. He was a particular friend of Arjuna, to whom he acted as charioteer in the great war, and his staunch support of the cause of the Pāṇḍavas was the main cause of the overthrow of the Kauravas. On several critical occasions, it was Kṛṣṇa's assistance and inventive mind that stood the Pāṇḍavas in good stead. After the general destruction of the Yādavas at Prabhāsa, he was killed unintentionally by a hunter named Jaras who shot him with an arrow mistaking him at a distance for a deer. He had more than 16000 wives, but Rukmini and Satyabhāmā, (as also Rādhā) were his favourites. He is said to have been of dark-blue or cloud-like colour; cf. बहिरिव मलिनतरं तव कृष्ण मनोपि भविष्यति नून Gīt. 8. कृष्ण—देव m. N. of a son of Nārāyaṇa (author of the Prayoga-sāra)
of a copyist (son of Paṇḍyā-puruṣottama-deva)
of another man, Inscr.
कृष्ण—द्र n. ? AV. ix, 7, 4.
कृष्ण—द्वादशी f. the twelfth day in the dark half of the month Aṣāḍha, VārP.

s: puM, (dvIpe Bava ityaR । yadvA dvIpaH ayanaM utpattisTAnaM yasya । prajYAdyaR । kfzRaScAsO dvEpAyanaSceti .) vedavyAsaH । iti trikARqaSezaH ॥ (yaTA, mahABArate 1 । 105 । 13 । “tatastasmin pratijYAte BIzmeRa kurunandana ! । kfzRadvEpAyanaM kAlI cintayAmAsa vE munim” ॥ asya yamunAdvIpotpattikaTA yaTA tatrEva 1 । 105 । 7 -- 14 । “Darmmayuktasya DarmmArTaM piturAsIttarI mama । sA kadAcidahaM tatra gatA praTamayOvane ॥ aTa DarmmavidAM SrezWaH paramarziH parASaraH । AjagAma tarIM DImAMstarizyan yamunAM nadIm ॥ sa tAryyamARo yamunAM mAmupetyAbravIttadA । sAntvapUrvvaM muniSrezWaH kAmArtto maDuraM vacaH ॥ tamahaM SApaBItA ca piturBItA ca BArata ! । varErasulaBEruktA na pratyAKyAtumutsahe ॥ aBiBUya sa mAM bAlAM tejasA vaSamAnayat । tamasA lokamAvftya nOgatAmeva BArata ! ॥ matsyaganDo mahAnAsIt purA mama jugupsitaH । tamapAsya SuBaM ganDamimaM prAdAt sa me muniH ॥ tato mAmAha sa munirgarBamutsfjya mAmakam । dvIpe'syA eva saritaH kanyEva tvaM Bavizyasi ॥ pArASaryyo mahAyogI sa baBUva mahAnfziH । kanyAputtro mama purA dvEpAyana iti SrutaH” ॥ anyat vivaraRAdikamasya vyAsaSabde drazwavyam ॥)
v: pu॰ dvIpe yamunAdvIpe BazaH Pak dvIpo'yanaM janmaBUmirvAsya prajYAdyaR karmma॰ । vedavyAse tasya yamunAdvIpotpattikaTA BA॰ A॰ 105 a॰ । “Darmmayuktasya DarmmArTaM piturAsIttarI mama । sA kadAcidahaM tatra gatA praTamayOvanA । aTa DarmavidA SrezWaH paramarziH parASaraH । AjagAma tarIM DImAMstarizyanyamunAM nadIm । sa tAryyamARo yamunAM mAmupetyAbravIttadA । sAntvapUrvaM muniSrezWaH kAmArtto maDuraM vacaH । tamahaM SApaBItA ca piturBItA ca BArata! । varErasulaBEruktA na pratyAKyAtusutsahe । aBiBUya sa mAM bAlAM tejasA vaSamAnayat । tamasA (kujJawikayA) lokamAvftya nOgatAmeba BArata! । matsvaganDo mahAnAsItpurA mama jugupsitaH । tamapAsya SuBaM ganDamimaM prAdAt sa me muniH । tato mAmAha sa munirgarBamutsfjya mAmakam । dvope'syA eva saritaH kanyEva tvaM Bavizyasi । pArASaryyo mahA yogI sa baBUva mahAnfziH । kanyAputro mama purA dvEpAyana iti SrutaH । yovyasya vedAMScaturastapasA BagavAnfziH । loke vyAsatvamApede kArzRyAt kfzRatvameva ca । satyavAdI SamaparastapasvI dagDakilvizaH । sadyotpannaH sa tu mahAn saha pitrA tato gataH” । “SrutvA tu sarpasatrAya dIkzitaM janamejayam । aByagacCadfzirvidvAn kfzRadvEpAyanastadA । janayAmAsa yaM kAlI SaktreH putrAtparASarAt । kanyEya yamunAdvIpe pARqavAnAM pitAmaham । jAtamAtraSca yaH sadya izwaM dehamavIvfDat । vedAMScADijage sANgAn setihAsAnmahAyaSAH । yannEti tapasA kaScinna vedADyayanena ca । na vratErnopavAsESca na prasUtyA na manyunA । vivyAsEkaM caturdDA yo vedaM vedavidAMvaraH । parAvarajYo brahmaziH kaviH satyavrataH SuciH । yaH pARquM DftarAzwraYca viduraM cApyajIjanat । SAntanoH santatiM tanvan puRyakIrttirmahAyaSAH” । “mAturniyogAdDarmAtmA gANgeyasya ca DImataH । kzetre vici travIryyasya kfzRadvEpAyanaH purA । trInagnIniva kOravyAn janayAmAsa vIryyavAn । utpAdya DftarAzwraYca pARquM vidurameva ca । jagAma tapase DImAn punarevASramaM prati” । “kfzRadvEpAyanAjjajYe DftarAzwro janeSvaraH । vicitravIryya kzetre ca pARquScEva mahAbalaH । DarmArTakuSalo DImAnmeDAvI DUtakalmazaH । viduraH SUdrayonO tu jajYe dvEpAyanAdapi” । BArate nAnAsTAna “kfzRadvEpAyanaM vyAsaM vidDi nArAyaRaM viBum । kohyanyaH puRqarIkzAt mahABAratakft Bavet” bizRupu॰ । tasya vizRo rabaratAratvakaTA BAga॰ “tataH saptadaSe jAtaH satyabatyAM parASarAt । cakre vedataroH SAKA dvApare so'lpameDasaH” । avatAraSabde 422 pf॰ vivftiH । kfzReti dvEpAyanoti ca tasya nAmadvayam karmma॰ kvacidekanAmatA'pi । “dvEpAyanena kfzRena nagare vAraRAvate” BA॰ sa॰ 76 a॰ । “kArzRyAt kfzRatvameva ca” “kArzRaM vedamimaM SfRu” iti ca byastaprayogaH । “tamahamarAgamatfzRaM kfzRadvEpAyanaM vandE” veRIsa॰ । prAguktaBArate ca samastaprayogaH
m: कृष्ण—द्वैपायन m. ‘black islander’, N. of Vyāsa (compiler of the MBh. and of the Purāṇas; so named because of his dark complexion and because he was brought forth by Satyavatī on a dvīpa or island in the Ganges), MBh.; Hariv.; Bādar. iii, 3, 32, Sch.; VP.
कृष्ण—गङ्गा f. the river Kistna (see कृष्णा), L.
कृष्ण—गल m. ‘having a black throat’, a kind of bird, Gal.

s: strI, (kfzRaH ugro ganDo yasyAH .) SoBAYjanaH । iti rAjanirGaRwaH ॥ (“imAMstrInaparAn vfkzAnAhuryezAM hitAMstvacaH । pUtikaH kfzRaganDA ca tillakaSca taTAtaruH ॥ virecane prayoktavyaH pUtikastillakastaTA । kfzRaganDA parIsarpe SoTezvarSaHsu cocyate” ॥ iti carake sUtrasTAne 1 aDyAye ॥
m: कृष्ण-गन्धा f. Hyperanthera Moringa, Suśr.

m: कृष्ण—गर्भा f. pl. the waters contained in the black cavities of the clouds [Comm. on Nir. iv, 24; ‘the pregnant wives of the Asura Kṛṣṇa’, Sāy.] RV. i, 101, 1.

s: puM, (kfzRaH kfzRavarRo garBaH aByantaradeSo yasya .) kawPalaH । iti rAjanirGaRwaH ॥
m: कृष्ण—गर्भ m. the plant Myrica sapida (= कट्फल), L.

v: pu॰ netrAvayavaBedakfzRagatarogaBede । tadvijYAnAdi suSrute uktaMyaTA । “aTAtaH kfzRagatarogavijYAnIyamaDyAyaM vyAKyAsyAmaH । yatsavraRaM SukramaTAvraRaM vA pAkAtyayaScAyajakA taTEva । catvAra ete'BihitAH vikArAH kfzRASrayAH saMgrahataH purastAt । nimagnarUpaM hi Bavettu kfzRe sUcyeva vidDaM pratiBAti yadvE । srAvaM sraveduzRamatIva ruk ca tatsavraRaM SukramudAharanti । dfzweH samIpe na Bavettu yacca na cAvagAQaM na ca saMsravedDi । avedanAvanna ca yugmaSukraM tatsidDimApnoti kadAcideva । sitaM yadA BAtyasitapradeSe syandAtmakaM nAtirugaSruyuktam । vihAyasIvABradalAnukAri tadavraRaM sADyatamaM vadanti । gamBIrajAtaM bahalaYca SuklaM cirotTitaYcApi vadanti kfcCram । vicCinnamaDyaM piSitAvftaM vA calaM sirAsaktamadfzwikfcca । dvitvaggataM lohitamantataSca cirotTitaYcApi vivarjjanIyam । uzRASrupAtaH piqakA ca kfzRe yasmin BavenmudganiBaYca Suklam । tadapyasADyaM pravadanti kecidanyacca yattittiripakzatulyam । saMCAdyate SvetaniBena sarvadozeRa yasyAsitamaRqalantu । ajApurIzapratimo rujAvAn salohito lohitapicCilAsraH । vidAryya kfzRaM pracayo'ByupEti taYcAjakAjAtamiti vyavasyet” ।
pu॰ kfzRA gatirgatisTAnamasya । kfzRavartmani vahnO tasya gamanasTAnasya tadgatyA kfzRatAprAptestasya taTAtvam । “vavfDe sa tadA garBaH kakze kfzRagatiryaTA” BA॰ Anu॰ 85 a॰ ।
m: कृष्ण—गति m. ‘whose way is black’, fire, MBh. xiii, 4071; Ragh. vi, 42.
कृष्ण—गव mfn. drawn by black oxen, ib.
कृष्ण—गिरि m. N. of a mountain, R. vi, 2, 34; Pāṇ. vi, 3, 117, Kāś.

कृष्ण—जी m. N. of a man.
कृष्ण—जीर m. Nigella indica (having a small black seed used for medical and culinary purposes), Bhpr.

s: puM, (kfzRaH kfzRavarRo jIrakaH .) kfzRavarRasTUlajIrakaH । kelejIrA iti BAzA । tatparyyAyaH । suzavI 2 kAravI 3 pfTvI 4 pfTuH 5 kAlA 6 upakuYcikA 7 । ityamaraH ॥ suSavI 8 kuYcikA 9 । iti tawwIkAyAM nayanAnandaH ॥ upakuYciH 10 । iti ratnamAlA ॥ kfzRA 11 jaraRA 12 SAlI 13 bahuganDA 14 । pfTukA 15 pfTivI 16 Bezajam 17 । iti SabdaratnA valI ॥ api ca । “kfzRajIraH suganDaSca taTEvodgAraSoDanaH । kaRAjAjI tu suzavI kAlikA copakAlikA ॥ pfTvIkA kAravI pfTvI pfTuH kfzRopakuYcikA । upakuYcI ca kuYcI ca vfhajjIraka ityapi ॥ jIrakatritayaM rUkzaM kadUzRaM dIpanaM laGu । saMgrAhi pittalaM meDyaM garBASayaviSudDikft ॥ jvaraGnaM pAcanaM balyaM vfzyaM rucyaM kaPApaham । cakzuzyaM pavanADmAnagulmacCardyatisArahft” ॥ iti BAvaprakASaH ॥ asya guRAH । kawutvam । uzRatvam । kaPaSoTajIrRajvaranASitvam । rucicakzurhitakAritvam । grAhitvaYca । iti rAjanirGaRwaH ॥ sa tu sTUlasUkzmaBedena dviDA ॥

v: pu॰ kfzRaprakAraH sTUlA॰ kan । 1 kfzRasarzape anukampitaM kfzRAjinam kan ajinAntatvAdattarapadalopaH । anukampite 2 kfzRAjine na॰

a: कृष्णकं — The hide of the black antelope.

कृष्ण—कर्मन् mfn. doing wrong, criminal, L.

a: कृष्ट — a. [कृष् कर्माणि क्त] 1 Drawn, pulled, dragged, attracted &c. --2 Ploughed; Pt. 1. 47. --Comp. --उप्त a. sown on cultivated ground. --पच्य, --पाक्य a. {1} ripening in cultivated. ground; cf. अकृष्टपच्य. {2} cultivated. --फलं the product of a harvest.

k.v: मौद्गीनकौद्रवीणादि शेषधान्योद्भवक्षमम्. शाकक्षेत्रादिके शाकशाकटं शाकशाकिनम्. बीजाकृतं तूप्तकृष्टे सीत्यं कृष्टं च हल्यवत्.।

m: कृष्ट—भूमि-जा f. (for कृष्ण-भ्˚?) a kind of grass, L.
कृष्ट—फल n. the product of a harvest, Yājñ. ii, 158.
कृष्ट—ज mfn. grown in cultivated ground, cultivated (as plants), Mn. xi, 144.
कृष्ट—मती-√ कृ (fr. मत्य), to plough and harrow, HPariś. ii, 357.

कृष्ट—राधि (कृष्ट-), mfn. successful in agriculture, AV. viii, 10, 24.

m: कृष्टि अयस्, f. pl. (once only sg. RV. iv, 42, 1) men, races of men (sometimes with the epithet मानुषीस् [i, 59, 5 and vi, 18, 2] or नाहुषीस् [vi, 46, 7] or मानवीस् [AV. iii, 24, 3]; cf. चर्षणि; originally the word may have meant cultivated ground, then an inhabited land, next its inhabitants, and lastly any race of men; Indra and Agni have the N. राजा or पतिः कृष्टीनाम्; the term पञ्च कृष्टयस्, perhaps originally designating the five Āryan tribes of the Yadus, Turvaśas, Druhyus, Anus, and Pūrus, comprehends the whole human race, not only the Āryan tribes), RV.; AV.
कृष्टि (इस्), f. ploughing, cultivating the soil, L.
attracting, drawing, L.
‘harvest’, the consequences (कर्म-क्˚), Naiṣ. vi, 100
कृष्टि (इस्), m. a teacher, learned man or Paṇḍit, Hariv. 3588; SkandaP.
a: कृष्टिः — [कृष्-क्तिन्] A learned man. --f. 1 Drawing, attracting. --2 Ploughing, cultivating the soil.

k.v: धीमान्सूरिः कृती कृष्टिर्लब्धवर्णो विचक्षणः। दूरदर्शी दीर्घदर्शी श्रोत्रियच्छान्दसौ समौ॥ मीमांसको जैमिनीये वेदान्ती ब्रह्मवादिनि। वैशेषिके स्यादौलूक्यः सौगतः शून्यवादिनि। नैयायिकस्त्वक्षपादः स्यात्स्याद्वादिक आर्हकः। चार्वाकलौकायतिकौ सत्कार्ये सांख्यकापिलौ।

m: कृष्टि—हन् mfn. subduing nations, ix, 71, 2.
कृष्टि—प्रा mfn. pervading the human race, RV. iv, 38, 9.
